feature: Every segmented control is the system's own
summary: Every row of side-by-side choices (panel rows, dialogs, the history bar's filter, the title bar's View | Edit) is now macOS's own segmented control, one continuous track that macOS draws. The drawn rail and sliding glass pane are gone.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Open any screen recording and look at View | Edit at the right of the title bar.
Click Edit, then View, then press Cmd-2 and Cmd-1.
Make a text layer, select it, and click Center and Right in the Text section's Across row.
Open the history bar (Shift-Cmd-H) and read the All / Screenshots / Videos filter in light and dark.
Compare every placement before and after on one sheet.
Pick a cut between two clips with a cross dissolve and use The overlap sits row in the Transition section.

evaluate: Is this the native control you meant, or did you expect a glass selection that slides between segments?
In the front window macOS fills the picked segment with your accent blue. Is that acceptable next to the rest of the app?
Does the title bar switch read as one control beside the panel button, not two loose buttons?
Is the picked word readable everywhere you look, the history filter included?
rough: macOS 26 does not slide the selection: filmed in front, Cmd-2 switches View to Edit from one frame to the next. The pointer film has no frames while the click is held, so a slide during a click cannot be ruled out there.
In a window in front the picked segment is accent blue, as macOS draws it; in a window behind it is grey. The drawn control's white glass pane is gone with the rest of it.
The Liquid Glass look Finder shows in its toolbar comes from a real window toolbar, which this editor deliberately does not have (it would draw a bar across the top). Not tried here.
The mock page comp-segmented.html was rewritten to document the system control, as this task asked; the mock set's own segmented.css still draws the old rail on other mock pages.
The old drawn control's thumb drag and its always-on keyboard focus are gone: arrows and Tab reach the control the way they do in every Mac app (Full Keyboard Access decides Tab).
